text:
Hi everyone,
I’m looking for some advice and, especially, experiences from couples who have been through the process of obtaining legal status/residency in Israel for a foreign spouse.

My wife is Israeli and I’m Italian, and we are already legally married. We are now preparing to start the process for me to live in Israel with her.

My situation is a little particular because of my job. I work in the maritime/cruise industry, and my position requires me to travel and work onboard ships regularly. Normally, I need to leave Israel for around 15 days at a time and then return, and this will continue to be my normal working pattern even after moving to Israel.

I’m therefore trying to understand how this can be managed during the spouse/residency process, especially since I understand that the authorities may expect the foreign spouse to actually reside in Israel and demonstrate that the couple’s “center of life” is in Israel.

Has anyone here been through a similar situation where the foreign spouse had to regularly leave Israel for work — for example, seafarers, airline crew, offshore workers, international employees, etc.?

I would really appreciate hearing about your experience:

• Did the frequent work-related travel create any problems with the process?

• How did you explain or document your work schedule to the Population and Immigration Authority?

• Were you able to continue the process normally while regularly leaving and re-entering Israel?

• Did you use an immigration lawyer, and if so, would you recommend them?

• Is there anything you wish you had known before starting the process?

We want to make sure we start everything correctly from the beginning and avoid problems later because of my work schedule.

Any personal experiences, recommendations, or lawyer contacts would be greatly appreciated.

Thank you very much!

Elhazov Lior
